welcome.title: Welcome to ClaudeDeck
welcome.subtitle: Manage several Claude Code accounts from one window, each kept fully separate.

accounts.title: Accounts
accounts.body: Each account runs as its own Claude Code profile, with its own settings, agents and sign-in.

projects.title: Projects
projects.body: Give each project a folder and an account; tabs opened in that project use that account.

tabs.title: Tabs
tabs.body: Open Claude and terminal tabs side by side in a project and pick up where you left off.

hooks.title: Hook status
hooks.managedOnly: Your organization's managed settings only allow managed hooks, so the test queue cannot work on this computer.
hooks.projectsDisabled: Hooks are disabled in these projects, so their tests are not queued: {{projects}}
hooks.bashOnly: The queue covers commands Claude runs with the Bash tool, including those of subagents.
hooks.bashOnlyWindows: The queue covers the Bash tool. Without Git Bash, Claude uses the PowerShell tool on this computer and the queue does not apply.

problem.noGitBash: The queue covers the Bash tool; this computer uses PowerShell because Git Bash is not installed, so no hook was added.
problem.invalidSettings: This account's settings.json is not valid JSON. ClaudeDeck does not change it; fix the file to install the hook.
problem.writeFailed: The hook could not be written to this account's settings.json.

settings.enabledHint: ClaudeDeck adds a hook to each account's Claude settings that makes test commands wait for a free slot. Turning this off removes the hook.

modeHint.fixed: A fixed number of tests run at the same time.
modeHint.auto: New tests start while CPU and memory have room.

settings.autoMaxHint: Leave empty to choose from the number of processor cores.
settings.maxWaitHint: After this, the test is turned away and Claude is told to run it again.
settings.cpuHighHint: No new test starts above this CPU usage.
settings.cpuResumeHint: Tests start again once CPU usage drops below this.
settings.minMemoryHint: No new test starts while less memory than this is available.
settings.rampUpHint: Lets the load of a new test show before the next one starts.
settings.startGraceHint: A started test with no sign of running frees its slot after this.
settings.backgroundHoldHint: Longest a background test without a visible process keeps its slot.

modeHint.inherit: Global rules apply, plus the changes below.
modeHint.off: Tests from this project's tabs never wait in the queue.

project.globalOff: The test queue is turned off in Settings; these choices apply once it is on.

permissions.title: Claude permissions
permissions.modeHint: Applies to Claude tabs started or restarted afterwards. Shift+Tab still switches modes inside a tab.

modeHints.default: No flag is passed; Claude's own settings choose the mode.
modeHints.manual: Claude asks before editing files or running commands.
modeHints.acceptEdits: File edits and common file commands run without asking.
modeHints.plan: Claude researches and proposes a plan without changing files.
modeHints.auto: A classifier reviews actions instead of asking you. Needs a supported plan and model.
modeHints.dontAsk: Only pre-approved tools run; anything else is denied without asking.
modeHints.bypassPermissions: Every command and edit runs without asking. Use only in trusted projects.

permissions.allowBypass: Allow switching to bypass with Shift+Tab
permissions.allowBypassHint: Tabs start in the chosen mode, and bypass permissions joins the Shift+Tab cycle. While it is available, plan mode no longer blocks edits.
permissions.testQueueNote: The test queue keeps working in every mode, bypass included: its hook runs before Claude's permission check.
permissions.projectHint: Used by this project's Claude tabs unless a tab was opened in a specific mode.
permissions.newTabMenu: Open Claude in a specific mode
permissions.tabBypass: Started in bypass permissions mode: Claude runs commands and edits without asking.

confirm.title: Bypass permissions?
confirm.risk: In this mode Claude runs every command and file edit without asking you, including deleting files, installing packages and pushing to git.
confirm.trust: Use it only in projects you trust, ideally isolated ones. Content Claude reads (web pages, files, issues) can steer it, and no prompt stops a harmful step.
confirm.claude: Claude also shows its own warning in the terminal the first time. Your deny rules and ClaudeDeck's test queue still apply.
